newsitem.title: south africa: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CONTINUE WINNING RUN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CONTINUE WINNING RUN.

text.p: Australia continued their all-conquering tour of South Africa with a 15-run win over an Eastern Province Invitation XI in the former township area of Zwide, near Port Elizabeth, on Tuesday.
It was their eighth win in eight matches on the tour so far and was set up by half centuries by Matthew Hayden (68), Justin langer (56) and Michael Bevan (57 not out).

Australia scored an imposing 243 for four in their 45 overs, but the E.P. team, containing a blend of seasoned first class players and young black cricketers, launched a bold chase for the runs and, at one stage, looked likely to upset the visitors.

Louis Koen, top domestic run scorer in South Africa for the last two seasons but ignored by the national selectors despite increasing calls for his inclusion, led the run chase with a classy 78 from 91 deliveries with 11 boundaries and a sx.
But when his fourth-wicket partnership of 47 with captain Dave Callaghan (25) was ended by Michael Bevan, the team's hopes of victory died too.

Earlier Hayden and Langer posted 112 effortless runs for the first wicket before Langer, who showed considerably more skill batting than he did filling in as a make-shift wicketkeeper, edged medium pacer Callaghan to wicketkeeper Lulama Mazikazaa. His 56 came from 70 balls with three fours and a six.
Hayden departed lbw attempting to sweep off-spinner Shafiek Abrahams for slightly less convincing 68 from 86 balls with seven fours and a six.
Bevan provided the necessary acceleration at the end of the innings with an inventive, unbeaten 57 from just 49 balls with five fours and a six.
Australia now begin final preparations for the second test against South Africa starting in Port Elizabeth on Friday. They won the first test in Johannesburg last week by and innings and 196 runs.
